hunks.sol: “Now you’re not even answering. You must never need to eat. Right? Chewing up other people’s words like that must fill you right—”

hunks.sol: As I turned away from the unconscious Woo Jintae, countless gazes flew toward me and fixed themselves upon me.

hunks.baseline: A murmur mixed with shock and fear spread through the room like a wave.

hunks.sol: There were more than a hundred guests on the first floor alone. It was hardly surprising that some of them recognized me.

hunks.baseline: “It’s the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi!”
hunks.sol: “I-it’s the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi!”

hunks.sol: “Do you think there are two Sleeping Dragons of Shanxi? I knew he looked familiar.”

hunks.sol: *My reputation as the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi really does shake the heavens.*

hunks.sol: “Are you sure? I saw the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi at Honghwaru around this time last year, but he looked a little…”

hunks.sol: “Yes. His build and overall impression have changed quite a bit, but it’s definitely him. I can still picture that young master from the Jin Family making an enormous scene because he wanted to bring a courtesan home with him.”

hunks.baseline: *Damn. Why do people remember such useless things?*
hunks.sol: *Damn. Why do people remember things like that?*

hunks.sol: As I awkwardly lowered my hand, several guests who had been whispering among themselves suddenly raised theirs.

hunks.sol: “I remember it clearly. That bastard—no, that gentleman—fell down the stairs, grabbed the thing between my legs, and gave it a long yank… Whew. Just thinking about it still makes me dizzy.”

hunks.baseline: I barely managed to suppress my urge to ask the man who had just spoken exactly how much longer it had gotten. There was still the trash from the so-called Five Gates of Shanxi to deal with.
hunks.sol: I barely suppressed the urge to ask exactly how much longer it had gotten. I still had the trash from the so-called Five Gates of Shanxi to deal with.

hunks.sol: Four young prodigies were lined up with their heads planted on the floor, while Hyuk Mujin stood beside them with his neck held strangely stiff.

hunks.sol: “They say even a village-school dog can recite poetry after three years. By now, I can tell what you want at a glance.”

hunks.baseline: I was seized by an indescribable emotion.
hunks.sol: An indescribable emotion seized me.

hunks.baseline: I was almost suspicious that he was putting points into Intelligence for me.
hunks.sol: I was starting to suspect he was putting points into Intelligence on my behalf.

hunks.sol: It was straight out of a historical drama. I took the sword case Hyuk Mujin held out and slapped it against my palm.

hunks.baseline: The grip was good, and the impact felt good, too.
hunks.sol: Good grip. Good impact, too.

hunks.baseline: “Everyone, get up.”
hunks.sol: “Everyone, on your feet.”

hunks.baseline: The four young prodigies sprang to their feet the moment I spoke.
hunks.sol: The four young prodigies sprang up the moment I spoke.

hunks.sol: Ignoring their terrified gazes, I scanned their Level Windows again. Just as I’d thought, they were barely First Rate, if that.

hunks.sol: “You’re not third sons or youngest daughters or anything like that?”

hunks.baseline: “No!”
hunks.sol: “No, sir!”

hunks.baseline: “Are you sure?”
hunks.sol: “You’re sure?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes, we are!”
hunks.sol: “Yes, sir!”

hunks.sol: Their disciplined shouts rang through the inn. I tapped the sword case against my palm and muttered,

hunks.sol: “What do you mean, no? You never had to worry about money, and you had powerful backing. You relied on that and strutted around like big shots, didn’t you? Picking fights wherever you went.”

hunks.baseline: “But then a war broke out between the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect. hunks.sol: “Then war broke out between the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect. The Jin Family had always treated you well, but you were afraid of the retaliation if Mount Heng won, so you watched from the sidelines until it was over. Right?”

hunks.baseline: “Th-that’s… We…”
hunks.sol: “Th-that’s… We don’t really…”

hunks.baseline: “You’re the heirs, aren’t you? A Young Sect Leader, a Lesser Family Head—something like that, right? Ah, that fellow over there was the Young Bureau Head.”
hunks.sol: “You’re the heirs, aren’t you? Young Sect Leaders, Lesser Family Heads, things like that. Ah, that fellow over there was the Young Bureau Head.”

hunks.baseline: The four people I pointed toward reflexively glanced in that direction and shuddered.
hunks.sol: The four of them reflexively followed my finger and shuddered.

hunks.baseline: Unable to endure the merciless barrage of slaps and trash talk, Woo Jintae had chosen to pass out. He lay on the floor as though he were dead.
hunks.sol: Unable to withstand the merciless barrage of slaps and trash talk, Woo Jintae had chosen to knock himself unconscious. He lay on the floor like a corpse.

hunks.baseline: “Anyway, given the situation, you should’ve kept your heads down. What did you come all the way here for, acting so high and mighty? Do you think the Jin Family of Taiyuan is a joke? Do I need to tattoo ‘Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi’ on my forehead and walk around with it?”
hunks.sol: “Anyway, given the situation, you should’ve kept your heads down. What possessed you to come all the way here and act so high and mighty? Do you think the Jin Family of Taiyuan is a joke? Do I need to tattoo ‘Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi’ across my forehead?”

hunks.baseline: “Does apologizing make everything go away? Should I beat you into a bloody mess and then apologize to you?”
hunks.sol: “Does apologizing make everything go away? Should I beat you into a bloody mess and apologize afterward?”

hunks.baseline: This was a situation that no longer required words. I raised the sword case.
hunks.sol: There was no need for any more words. I raised the sword case.

hunks.baseline: “Historically, this has always been an effective remedy. Everyone, get down.”
hunks.sol: “Historically, this has always been the best medicine. Everyone, get down.”

hunks.baseline: Then I asked the four trembling young prodigies who lay face down in a chilling voice,
hunks.sol: Then I asked the four trembling young prodigies lying face down before me in a chilling voice,

hunks.sol: “Give me a number. Woo Jintae got beaten that badly because he was too full of himself. Since you paid up voluntarily, I’ll take that into consideration.”

hunks.baseline: The four of them exchanged hurried glances before shouting as one.
hunks.sol: The four exchanged hurried glances, then shouted in unison.

hunks.baseline: I gripped the sword case tightly.
hunks.sol: I tightened my grip on the sword case.

hunks.baseline: Back in school, I felt like one of those physical-education entrance-exam teachers who swung a bat whenever he got the chance.
hunks.sol: I felt like one of those physical-education entrance-exam instructors from my school days who swung a bat whenever he got the chance.

hunks.baseline: Wallowing in a strange sense of nostalgia, I swung the bat—or rather, the sword case.
hunks.sol: Sinking into a strange sense of nostalgia, I swung the bat—or rather, the sword case.

hunks.sol: The whispers of the crowd surrounding us reached my ears.
